name: New York City
summary: New York began as New Amsterdam, a Dutch fur-trading post founded on Manhattan in 1624 and seized by the English forty years later. The Erie Canal made it the nation's greatest port; the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island made it the gateway for millions of immigrants; Wall Street made it the capital of American finance. Consolidated into five boroughs in 1898 and home to the United Nations since 1945, it endured the Crash of 1929 and the attacks of September 11, 2001, and remains the largest and most influential city in the United States.

events.title: Henry Hudson
events.body: Sailing for the Dutch, Henry Hudson explores the river that now bears his name.

events.title: New Amsterdam
events.body: The Dutch found a fur-trading post on the tip of Manhattan.

events.title: Manhattan “purchased”
events.body: Peter Minuit acquires Manhattan from the Lenape for a bundle of trade goods.

events.title: The wall on Wall Street
events.body: The Dutch build a defensive wall along the line of today’s Wall Street.

events.title: The English take over
events.body: An English fleet seizes the colony and renames it New York.

events.title: Revolution and occupation
events.body: Washington loses the Battle of Brooklyn; the British hold New York through the Revolution.

events.title: Capital of the nation
events.body: New York briefly serves as the capital of the new United States.

events.title: Washington inaugurated
events.body: George Washington is sworn in as the first president on Wall Street.

events.title: The grid
events.body: The Commissioners’ Plan lays out Manhattan’s famous rectangular street grid.

events.title: The Erie Canal
events.body: The canal makes New York the gateway to the interior and the nation’s greatest port.

events.title: Central Park
events.body: Work begins on Central Park, a vast green space amid the exploding city.

events.title: The Draft Riots
events.body: Violent, racist anti-draft riots convulse the city during the Civil War.

events.title: The Brooklyn Bridge
events.body: The great suspension bridge finally links Manhattan and Brooklyn.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty
events.body: France’s colossal gift is dedicated in New York harbour.

events.title: Ellis Island opens
events.body: The immigration station begins processing millions of newcomers to America.

events.title: The five boroughs
events.body: New York consolidates into a single city of five boroughs.

events.title: The subway
events.body: The first line of the New York City Subway opens.

events.title: The Wall Street Crash
events.body: The stock market collapses, beginning the Great Depression.

events.title: The Empire State Building
events.body: The world’s tallest building opens in the depths of the Depression.

events.title: Capital of the world
events.body: The new United Nations chooses New York for its headquarters.

events.title: Stonewall
events.body: A police raid at the Stonewall Inn sparks the modern gay-rights movement.

events.title: Blackout and crisis
events.body: A blackout, a fiscal crisis and rising crime mark the city’s hardest years.

events.title: Renewal
events.body: Crime falls sharply and the city rebounds through the 1990s.

events.title: September 11
events.body: Hijacked planes destroy the World Trade Center, killing nearly 3,000 people.

events.title: Hurricane Sandy
events.body: A superstorm floods much of the low-lying city.
